name: Sky Grey
lede: Sky Grey is a pale bluish-white first dated by Ridgway in 1912, closest in our library to Silver and built on the same root word as Sky Blue.

sections.title: A 1912 landscape word
sections.body: ColorHub's library traces Sky Grey to Ridgway's 1912 color standard (plate XXXIV, hue 45′′) and classes it, in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, as a very pale green, block 148 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary carries the same name on plate 34 B2, also dated to 1912 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-neropalin-blue]], [[burn-blue]], [[pale-russian-blue]] and [[pale-aqua]], at 2.5, 3.9, 5, 3.9, 4.9 and 4.9 ΔE [1]. [[periwinkle]] and [[grey]] turn up far more often than chance in paintings that also carry this color, alongside [[slate-grey]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a close match to Sky Grey in 357 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.5 percent, as photographed [2]. It plays a highlight in 94 percent of those appearances, the pale note at the top of a tone, not a shadow or a midtone [2]. Gaspard Dughet, Carlos de Haes and Camille Pissarro all use it well above the archive's average rate [2].

The earliest dated match is a 1401 Madonna and Child by Lorenzo di Niccolò, four centuries before Ridgway recorded the name, which only shows a similar screen color was photographed there, not that anyone called it Sky Grey, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].

disambiguation.gloss: same root word, a saturated mid-blue rather than a near-white grey
